title: The Tools
logline: A fisherman's nets, mended and re-mended for thirty years, pass to his son, whose hands are shaped by the same work before he has fully learned it.
human_question: What actually continues when someone's life's work passes to someone else?

premise.story: The tools and trade of a fisherman who has recently died, now in daily use by the relative who has taken up his work: nets, a boat, the particular knots and habits of the trade.
premise.place: A fishing village on the west coast.
premise.experience: Salt-worn hands on old nets, a boat that still carries one man's habits of repair, and a successor learning a trade that is also, quietly, a form of company with someone gone.

concept_links.why: Both sources insist that nothing physical or mental travels from one life to the next, yet what follows is never a stranger, only ever what the causal stream itself produces [C061-P:L85; C061-M:L15-L17]. Tools passing into someone else's hands, worn into the shape of the first person's use, give that continuity-without-a-traveller an entirely ordinary, secular form.
What a person leaves unfinished, including a trade only partly handed on, is part of what the source calls a life's continuing, unresolved action [C057-P:L87].

what_camera_could_observe: The tools themselves, worn to one person's grip
The successor learning or continuing the trade
The day's catch or the day's work brought home
what_must_be_real: A real family's real trade and real loss. The film does not claim anything about how the person died or what, if anything, they 'saw' at the end.

possible_arc.opening: The tools at rest, still shaped by one person's hands.
possible_arc.turn: The successor at work, learning what the tools still teach.
possible_arc.ending_open: A day's work completed. The trade continues, changed by whoever now does it.

position_hint: closing candidate: continuity carried entirely by ordinary work and objects, without doctrine, a plain image for what the group's teaching on rebirth holds without a traveller

requirements: A fishing family who has recently lost the person whose trade and tools are now used by a relative
Willingness to be filmed at real, ongoing work

suggestions.name: A fishing village near Negombo
suggestions.why: An established west-coast fishing community; no specific family identified.
suggestions.verify: No family confirmed; would need direct outreach and consent.

risks: Implying anything about the cause or manner of the original owner's death
Turning a working trade into a metaphor rather than a livelihood
drop_if: No family with this exact situation and full consent can be found
The successor does not want their inherited trade framed around the death

connections.note: Both follow an object outliving the person who used it, one at the very start of the group, one much later.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
